judged_text: The 60-second throttle key is written to redis (setnx + expire) inside retrieved_recently? before perform_retrieve runs, so the key is committed before the retrieval operation has succeeded. When perform_retrieve raises (network error, 404, readability failure), the key persists for 60 seconds so every subsequent retry job executes retrieve, hits retrieved_recently? and returns silently — retries no-op 'successfully' while no topic is created, and the failure is never surfaced to anyone.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The 60-second throttle key is written to redis (setnx + expire) inside retrieved_recently? before perform_retrieve runs, so the key is committed before the retrieval operation has succeeded. When perform_retrieve raises (network error, 404, readability failure), the key persists for 60 seconds so every subsequent retry job executes retrieve, hits retrieved_recently? and returns silently — retries no-op 'successfully' while no topic is created, and the failure is never surfaced to anyone.

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/topic_retriever.rb`, `retrieve` calls `perform_retrieve` only if `retrieved_recently?` is false. But `retrieved_recently?` writes the throttle key first (`$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` + `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`) and then returns `false` to allow `perform_retrieve` to run. If `perform_retrieve` (e.g., `fetch_http` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `open(url).read` / Readability parsing) raises, nothing clears the key. Subsequent retries within 60s will hit `retrieved_recently?` (now true) and skip `perform_retrieve`, causing retry jobs to no-op without creating the topic.
